about: Simplified Technical English wording for the Mars data files (mars.json, mars_extra.json, mars_environment.json): the sentences that the Mars section, the place card and the search show.

mars.json.1 at 25 mm of rain and snow a year or le: The score is 1 at 25 mm of rain and snow a year or less. The score is 0 at 500 mm or more. Between these two points, the score follows a straight line on a log scale.
mars.json.1 where the square's yearly mean air tem: The score is 1 if the yearly mean air temperature of the square is equal to that of the site, or colder. The score is 0 at +30 C or warmer. Between these two points, the score follows a straight line.
mars.json.668.6 sols of 24.66 h; seasons nearly tw: The Mars year has 668.6 sols of 24.66 h. Its seasons are almost two times as long as on Earth, and they are not equal in length (orbit eccentricity 0.0935, against 0.0167). Thus one Earth month represents approximately two Mars months.
mars.json.Among bare ground, the scores do not pic: If the check uses only bare squares, the scores do not separate the places that scientists studied from the other squares.
mars.json.By formula from the site's latitude (pla: These values come from a formula that uses the latitude of the site (planetocentric) and the tilt of Mars, 25.19 degrees. Over the Mars year, the declination of the Sun changes between -25.19 and +25.19 degrees. Noon Sun height = 90 - |latitude - declination|. Thus the lowest is 90 - (|latitude| + 25.19), and a value below 0 means polar night. The highest is 90 if |latitude| <= 25.19; if not, it is 90 - (|latitude| - 25.19). Day length = 2 H0 / 360 x 24.66 h, with cos H0 = -tan(latitude) tan(declination), at declination -25.19 and +25.19 (0 h in polar night, 24.66 h in polar day). A Mars solar day is 24.66 Earth hours. The values are for the centre of the Sun on a flat horizon, without refraction and without terrain. The seasons of Mars are not equal in length (orbit eccentricity 0.093). This changes when the Sun gets to a height, not how high it goes.
mars.json.Curiosity studies this crater while driv: Curiosity studies this crater and drives uphill from its landing point.
mars.json.Curiosity's weather figures are from NAS: Curiosity's weather figures come from NASA's public weather feed. The feed says that it is for outreach. These figures are not archive data.
mars.json.Earth climate comes from a grid-box mode: Earth climate comes from a grid-box model, not from measurements at each square. The yearly mean temperatures on Mars also come from a model.
mars.json.Every half-degree Earth square with at l: This file gives the scores of each Earth square of half a degree with at least 15 % bare ground, against each Mars site.
mars.json.Its REMS station has recorded air temper: Its REMS station records air temperature, ground temperature and pressure.
mars.json.Known sites were partly picked for bare: Teams selected the known sites partly because they have bare and dry ground. Thus the check against all land is partly circular.
mars.json.Mars air is 95.1 % CO2, 2.59 % N2, 1.94: The air of Mars is 95.1 % CO2, 2.59 % N2, 1.94 % Ar, 0.16 % O2 and 210 ppm water. The air of Earth is 78.08 % N2, 20.95 % O2 and 420 ppm CO2. The mean molecular weight is 43.49 on Mars, against 28.97 on Earth.
mars.json.Mars has almost no ozone, so UV-C (200-2: Mars has almost no ozone. Thus UV-C (200-280 nm) reaches the surface of Mars, but it never reaches the ground of Earth. On Mars, only CO2 stops light shorter than approximately 190-200 nm.
mars.json.Mars-wide 6.36 mb (636 Pa) at the mean r: The mean for all of Mars is 6.36 mb (636 Pa) at the mean radius. The pressure changes from 400 to 870 Pa with place and season (Mars Fact Sheet).
mars.json.Mars: dose equivalent measured by Curios: Mars: Curiosity RAD measured a dose equivalent of 0.64 +/- 0.12 mSv/day at Gale (absorbed dose 0.21 mGy/day). Earth: the world mean natural background is approximately 2.4 mSv/year.
mars.json.Mars: optical depth generally below 1 in: Mars: the optical depth is usually below 1 in the aphelion season (Ls 0-180). It is above 3 at the peak of global dust storms (record of 7 landers on the surface). Dust is in the sky all year. Earth: the global mean optical depth at 550 nm is approximately 0.1-0.2. This Earth figure is from memory and is not checked.
mars.json.Mars: this site's yearly mean, measured: Mars: the yearly mean at this site, measured by a lander (Curiosity REMS, daily minimum and maximum air temperature and daily pressure). Earth: standard sea-level pressure. Lowest land square: the yearly mean surface pressure (PS) of NASA POWER in this file.
mars.json.Mars: this site's yearly mean, model (mo: Mars: the yearly mean at this site, from a model (Mars Climate Database v6.2, LMD with ESA and CNES, web interface). Earth: standard sea-level pressure. Lowest land square: the yearly mean surface pressure (PS) of NASA POWER in this file.
mars.json.NASA has selected no human landing site: NASA does not have a selected site for a human landing on Mars.
mars.json.Orbital radar indicates that debris apro: Radar from orbit shows that the debris aprons around the mesas contain water ice under a rocky cover.
mars.json.These factors do not measure chemistry,: These factors do not measure chemistry, minerals, ice or life. Many coordinates of known sites are estimates.
mars.json.These smooth northern plains may hold ab: Scientists think that these smooth northern plains hold a large quantity of shallow water ice.
mars.json.This check asks whether known analog squ: This check shows if known analog squares rank higher than control squares.
mars.json.any unknown factor makes the goal unknow: If a factor is unknown, the goal is unknown. If a factor is 0, the goal is 0.
mars.json.first pass: squares of 0.5 degree (about: This is a first pass. Its squares are 0.5 degree wide, approximately 55 km. On both planets, the heights are 1.85 km apart and each slope covers approximately 3.7 km. The first pass is coarser than the Moon part.
mars.json.geometric mean of dry, cold and bare: The score is the geometric mean of the dry, cold and bare scores.
mars.json.geometric mean of terrain and bare: The score is the geometric mean of the terrain and bare scores.
mars.json.geometric mean of terrain, dry, cold, ba: The score is the geometric mean of the terrain, dry, cold, bare and sun scores.
mars.json.literature, not checked against a saved: From the literature, not checked against a saved file in this run. Mars: study published in 2000, Icarus 146, 343-359. Earth: the ozone cut-off near 290 nm.
From the literature, not checked against a saved file in this run. Mars: study published in 2014, Science 343, 1244797 (RAD). Earth: UNSCEAR 2008.
mars.json.measured by a lander (Curiosity REMS, da: Measured by a lander: Curiosity REMS, daily minimum and maximum air temperature and daily pressure, sols 1 to 4995. These values come from NASA's weather feed, which carries the CAB note 'for outreach purposes only'. The scientific record is the REMS data in PDS, which we did not read. Model: Mars Climate Database v6.2 (LMD with ESA and CNES), web interface, climatology average solar scenario. The values are for 2 m above the surface, in steps of 15 degrees of Ls and 1 hour of local time.
mars.json.measured by a lander (Phoenix MET, PDS l: Measured by a lander: Phoenix MET, PDS low-rate reduced files, 1000 mm mast sensor, sols 0 to 151, Ls 77 to 148, northern summer only. Model: Mars Climate Database v6.2 (LMD with ESA and CNES), web interface, climatology average solar scenario. The values are for 2 m above the surface, in steps of 15 degrees of Ls and 1 hour of local time.
mars.json.min(1, overlap of the square's and the s: The score is the overlap of the slope histograms of the square and of the site, divided by the overlap of the site with itself. The maximum score is 1.
mars.json.model (Mars Climate Database v6.2, LMD w: Model: Mars Climate Database v6.2 (LMD with ESA and CNES), web interface, climatology average solar scenario. The values are for 2 m above the surface, in steps of 15 degrees of Ls and 1 hour of local time.
mars.json.nm, shortest wavelength of sunlight reac: nm, the shortest wavelength of sunlight that reaches the ground
mars.json.per month, the geometric mean of that mo: For each month, the score is the geometric mean of three values. Cold compares the monthly mean air temperature with the yearly mean of the site, on the same scale (0 at +30 C or warmer). Dry uses the precipitation of the month times 12. The third value is 1 if the noon Sun height of the square on the 15th of the month is in the yearly range of the site. If not, it is 0.
mars.json.the bare share of the square's land: The score is the share of the land in the square that is bare.
mars.json.the share of the site's yearly range of: The score is the share of the yearly range of noon Sun height at the site that the yearly range of the square covers. Both planets use absolute latitude. The tilt is 25.19 degrees on Mars and 23.44 degrees on Earth.
mars.json.the three months with the highest month: These are the three months with the highest month scores above 0. The best month is first. Months with equal scores stay in calendar order.

mars_extra.json.Measured by digging at the site: the pap: The lander measured this depth in trenches that it dug at the site. The abstract of the paper tells of '3-5 cm deep icy soil interfaces' in the trenches. NASA's photojournal for the Dodo-Goldilocks trench (dug 12 June 2008, 7 to 8 cm deep) shows white material in its upper part. Later, this material was found to be ice.

mars_extra.json.No public figure found. Jezero (18.4 N): We found no public figure. Jezero (18.4 N) is inside the SWIM study area, but we could not get SWIM's map files tonight. Fig. 1a of the paper puts the theoretical 3 m zone of ice stability far from the site, in the direction of the pole.
mars_extra.json.No published record of dune movement or: Tonight we did not open a published record of dune movement or slope streaks at this site. JPL news pages refused scripted requests (HTTP 403). The value is empty, not zero.
mars_extra.json.No single depth is published. For the gl: No publication gives a single depth. For the glaciers of Deuteronilus Mensae, the paper gives two readings. The ice is under a very thin debris cover of less than 2 m, or under meters of highly porous material. SWIM's map files did not answer tonight (HTTP 523).
mars_extra.json.No single depth is published. The SWIM p: No publication gives a single depth. The SWIM paper concludes that ice is 'present close to the surface in Arcadia'. It maps a radar reflector at depths of 15 to more than 100 m and reads it as the base of an ice-bearing layer. SWIM's own map files (swim.psi.edu) did not answer tonight (HTTP 523). Thus we read no value at the coordinates of the site.
mars_extra.json.Nobody has drilled or measured heat here: This class does not come from a drill hole or from a heat measurement here. It only says that hot rock is probably near the surface. A place far from volcanoes can also have useful warm ground (deep basins, hot springs), and a place near a volcano can be unusable. Tonight we did not find an open map of geothermal potential for the world that we could get without a login. The list of plants stops in approximately 2021 and does not include some plants.
mars_extra.json.Not a count of rocks or boulders and not: This is not a count of rocks or boulders, and it is not a rock abundance of the Diviner type. The 90 m height data of Earth cannot see single rocks. The slopes and the roughness are for a window of 10 km (Moon part) or a square of 55 km (Mars part). The rock map gives one class for a box of approximately 55 km.
mars_extra.json.Not a depth: a class from the permafrost: This is not a depth. It is a class from the permafrost zone only, with no metres. The thaw depth changes from metre to metre with soil, water and plants.
mars_extra.json.Not a detection. Ilmenite also occurs in: This is not a detection. Ilmenite also occurs in gabbro and other rocks. Most basalt holds only a few per cent of it. The class 'possible' means only that the rock type can hold iron-titanium oxide.
mars_extra.json.Not a hazard map and not a forecast. It: This is not a hazard map and not a forecast. It counts the earthquakes of magnitude 5 and above in the USGS catalogue from 1 January 1990 to 31 December 2025. Each epicentre is within 200 km of the centre of the place. These are 36 years of a catalogue, not the ground motion that a site can expect. The count does not include smaller earthquakes, which people can still feel. It does not use depth: a deep earthquake 200 km away counts the same as a shallow one. The magnitudes are the preferred values of the catalogue, of mixed types (mw, mb, ms, ...), thus 'magnitude 5' is not one scale everywhere. The count does not include events that the catalogue gives a type other than 'earthquake' (nuclear explosions, volcanic eruptions, a mine collapse, a landslide).
mars_extra.json.Not a population map and not a noise or: This is not a population map, and it is not a measurement of noise or light. Each distance is a straight line, not a travel distance. GeoNames cities1000 lists places of more than 1,000 people and seats of local government, thus camps, stations, mines and hamlets are not in the list. Natural Earth holds only main roads and railways. Thus if a road is not in the data, this is not proof that there is no road: tracks, winter roads and mine roads are mostly absent. We know only that an airfield exists, not its traffic.
mars_extra.json.Not an observation of moving dunes or du: This is not an observation of dunes that move or of dust storms. The wind is a monthly mean at 10 m, not the gusts that move sand. If sand moves or not depends on grain size and crusts, and we do not have these data.
mars_extra.json.Not filled tonight. The global rock-abun: We did not fill this value tonight. We found the global maps of rock abundance only as coloured pictures (ASU's WMS PNG and JMARS layer), not as a numeric file on PDS or USGS Astrogeology. We did not find the TES rock-abundance map (Nowicki & Christensen 2007) as a download. We did not read numbers back from the colours.
mars_extra.json.Not hydrogen content and not percent wat: This is not a hydrogen content and not a percent of water. It is a model wetness (0 dry to 1 saturated) of the top 5 cm in a MERRA-2 grid box. The rule divides it into thirds relative to the places of the same file. Ground ice comes from a 1 km model of permafrost probability, not from a borehole.
mars_extra.json.Not read from spectra and not a sample a: This does not come from spectra, and it is not an analysis of a sample. It gives the usual minerals of the rock-map class for a box of approximately 55 km, or of a listed anorthosite body. The map has no anorthosite class. Thus the rule misses bodies that are not on our list.
mars_extra.json.Not sunlight at the ground: what a level: This is not sunlight at the ground. It is what a level surface would get above the atmosphere. We keep it to compare the ground figures with it.
mars_extra.json.Not thermal inertia. The swing is that o: This is not thermal inertia. The swing is that of the air 2 m above the ground, in a MERRA-2 grid box of approximately 55 km. The albedo is that of a CERES box of 1 degree. Cloud, humidity, wind and the sea decrease the swing as much as the ground does. Thus a place on a coast can read 'slow' because of the sea, not because of the rock. The thirds are relative to the places of the same file.
mars_extra.json.Not what a tilted or tracking panel woul: This is not the output of a tilted panel or of a panel that follows the Sun. It is not a measurement at the place, and it is not the light of the hours of low Sun only. The value is for a coarse box of approximately 111 km by 20 to 55 km at these latitudes.
mars_extra.json.Not what reaches the ground on a typical: This is not what reaches the ground on a typical day. It is what would reach a level surface on the same days if there were no cloud.

The wind moves Namib Dune forward by approximately one meter a year. This is the dune field near the route of the rover, not the landing point itself.
mars_extra.json.The PDS product leaves this 5 deg bin bl: The PDS product leaves this 5 deg bin blank (9999.999, 'not applicable'). It does the same for the other high-latitude bins that we checked (62.5 and 67.5 N). This map gives no value at this site. The Phoenix lander itself dug to ice (see Depth to water ice).
mars_extra.json.The calendar months whose mean air tempe: These are the calendar months with a mean air temperature above 0 C at 2 m above the ground, in the NASA POWER grid. The Moon part uses temperature_cells.json, and the Mars part uses mars_climate.json. If no month is above 0 C, the rule uses the warmest month only. The rule uses temperature, not the snow maps, to make sure that the Moon part and the Mars part use the same rule.
mars_extra.json.a listed settlement of 1,000 or more peo: If a listed settlement of 1,000 or more people is within 5 km, steady human disturbance is likely. The same class applies if a main road or railway is within 2 km, or if an airfield with scheduled flights is within 10 km.
mars_extra.json.a listed settlement of any size lies wit: If a listed settlement of any size is within 25 km, human disturbance is possible. The same class applies if a main road or railway is within 10 km, or if an airfield of any kind is within 10 km.
mars_extra.json.a volcano that erupted in 3 or more sepa: If a volcano within 30 km of the centre erupted in 3 or more separate years since 1990, steady volcanic effects are likely. If such a volcano erupted at any time since 2015, they are also likely.
mars_extra.json.a volcano that erupted since 1990 lies w: If a volcano within 100 km erupted since 1990, volcanic effects come and go.
mars_extra.json.active dunes, about 1 m per year: active dunes, approximately 1 m per year
mars_extra.json.close to the surface (published words);: close to the surface (published words); an ice-bearing layer to a depth of 15 to >100 m
mars_extra.json.dry, moist or wet by thirds of the mean: The class is dry, moist or wet, by thirds of the mean top-soil wetness over the snow-free months (NASA POWER GWETTOP, 0 dry to 1 saturated). The thirds come from the places of each output file (the cut values are in meta.cuts). If the grid point of the model is ice (soil_wetness_ice_flag), the value is unknown. Ground ice is likely if the mean permafrost probability is 0.5 or more, possible from 0.1 to less than 0.5, and unlikely below 0.1. In Antarctica, ground ice is likely, from the literature note of rock_frozen_cells.json (not a map value). If the map has no value and the yearly mean air temperature is 3 C or more, ground ice is unlikely. In other places without a map value, the value is unknown.
mars_extra.json.from the permafrost zone: continuous ->: The class comes from the permafrost zone: continuous -> shallow; discontinuous -> shallow in most of the area; sporadic -> patchy; isolated patches -> rare; none -> none expected; Antarctica -> shallow (literature). If the map has no value and the yearly mean air temperature is 3 C or more, the class is none expected (as in rule 4). In other places without a map value, the value is unknown. The rule gives classes only, not metres. The open pages that we read tonight gave no rule of thumb for each zone for the thickness of the layer that thaws in summer (meta.frozen_ground_depth_sources).
mars_extra.json.high when at least 0.5 of the land is ba: The class is high if three conditions are true. At least 0.5 of the land is bare. The ground is steep or rough. The rock map does not say loose sediment. Steep or rough means a 90th-percentile slope of 10 degrees or more. It can also mean a roughness at 90 m that is not less than that of the smoothest lunar region. The class is low if less than 0.25 of the land is bare. It is also low if the rock map says loose sediment and the 90th-percentile slope is less than 5 degrees. If not, the class is medium. The Mars part has no roughness at 90 m, thus only the slope test decides if the ground is steep or rough. Its slopes cover approximately 3.7 km, thus they show flatter ground than the 90 m slopes of the Moon part.
mars_extra.json.ice-free ground there is permafrost thro: The literature says that the ice-free ground there is permafrost throughout. This is not in our data.
mars_extra.json.in how many of the 16 years at least one: The number of years, of the 16 years, with at least one such event in the catalogue within 100 km. This number shows if the events are consistent: 14 of 16 is steady, and 1 of 16 is one swarm. If the catalogue cannot see small tremors here, the value is unknown.
mars_extra.json.index = mean of (1 - albedo) over the sn: index = the mean of (1 - albedo), divided by the mean daily temperature swing of the air at 2 m. Both means use the snow-free months where both values are known. The unit is 1 per degree C. The index divides the places of each output file into thirds. The lowest third gets 'heats and cools fast, like dry dust or sand'. The middle third gets 'in between'. The highest third gets 'slow, like rock or wet ground'. Both inputs come from coarse climate grids (NASA POWER: CERES 1 degree albedo, MERRA-2 air temperature swing), not from the ground at the place.
mars_extra.json.likely where the ground is loose sedimen: The class is likely if three conditions are true. The ground is loose sediment (rock map) or mostly bare (bare share 0.5 or more). The top soil is in the dry third. The mean wind at 10 m over the snow-free months is 6 m/s or more. The class is unlikely if the top soil is in the wet third, or if the ground is frozen. Frozen means that the grid point of the model is ice, or that the rock map says ice and glaciers. The class is also unlikely if the ground is mostly not bare (bare share less than 0.25: plants, ice or water). If not, the class is possible.
mars_extra.json.literature note (Antarctica), not a map: A note in the literature (Antarctica), not a map value.
mars_extra.json.mean number a year of catalogued events: The mean number of catalogued events a year, of magnitude 2.5 to less than 5, within 50 km of the centre of the place, 2010-2025. If the catalogue cannot see small tremors here, the value is unknown.
mars_extra.json.median slope, degrees, over a span of ab: The median slope in degrees. Each slope covers approximately 3.7 km, and the heights are 1.85 km apart. On Earth, the median uses the land of the square (0.5 degree, approximately 55 km from north to south). On Mars, it uses the 2 x 2 degree box of the site (approximately 118 km).

mars_extra.json.our rough estimate: the catalogue cannot: Our rough estimate, because the catalogue cannot see small tremors here.
mars_extra.json.our rule of thumb, not an engineering st: This is our rule of thumb, not an engineering standard. The class is 'steady small tremors' if catalogued events occurred within 100 km in at least 12 of the 16 years. The rate must also be at least 5 a year. The class is 'occasional small tremors' if at least one event occurred within 100 km, but not steadily. That is, in 1 to 11 of the years, or less than 5 a year. Events in 1 to 3 years are usually a single swarm. The class is 'none recorded' if the catalogue records small tremors here and has no event within 100 km. The class is 'cannot tell' if the catalogue cannot see small tremors here. It is also 'cannot tell' if the catalogue sees only tremors above a magnitude between 2.5 and 3.5 and has no event within 100 km. Then an empty circle tells nothing about smaller tremors.
mars_extra.json.possible where the rock map says basic v: The class is possible if the rock map says basic volcanic rock, or if the place is on a listed anorthosite body. Deposits of iron-titanium oxide occur in both. If not, the class is unlikely. If the map says ice, water or no data and no body is listed, the value is unknown.
mars_extra.json.read from the rock map's class by one ta: One table (meta.mineral_family_table) gives the family from the class of the rock map. Basic volcanic rock gives 'basalt minerals (plagioclase, pyroxene, olivine): like the Moon's dark plains and like Mars'. A place on a listed anorthosite body (data/reference/anorthosite_bodies.json) gives 'plagioclase-rich: like the Moon's bright highlands', with the listed feldspar composition of the body (An number). This result has priority over the class of the map. Each other class gets its usual minerals in a few plain words. For boxes with ice, water or no data, the value is unknown. The rule reads a rock map, not spectra.
mars_extra.json.south of 25 N: outside the map, which co: South of 25 N: this place is outside the map. The map covers land from 25 N to the north.
mars_extra.json.southern hemisphere outside Antarctica:: Southern hemisphere outside Antarctica: this is not in our data, because the map covers only the north. Mountain permafrost can exist there at high altitude.
mars_extra.json.sum of the listed populations of the set: The sum of the listed populations of the settlements with a point within 25 km. The value is 0 if no settlement is listed. It is unknown if settlements are listed but none has a figure. It is a lower bound if only some settlements have no figure.
mars_extra.json.sum of the listed populations within 100: The sum of the listed populations within 100 km. The value is 0 if no settlement is listed there. It is unknown if settlements are listed but none gives a figure. It is a lower bound if only some have no figure (see settlements_without_population_within_100km).

mars_extra.json.uv_index is the service's ALLSKY_SFC_UV_: The UV index (uv_index) is ALLSKY_SFC_UV_INDEX of the service. It is a mean over all 24 hours of the day, and it includes the night. The UV index of the brightest hour (uv_index_brightest_hour) is the highest hourly value of ALLSKY_SFC_UV_INDEX_HR for the mean day of each month.

mars_environment.json.Mars has almost no ozone, so UV-C (200-2: Mars has almost no ozone. Thus UV-C (200-280 nm) reaches the surface of Mars, but it never reaches the ground of Earth. On Mars, only CO2 stops light shorter than approximately 190-200 nm.
mars_environment.json.Mars: optical depth generally below 1 in: Mars: the optical depth is usually below 1 in the aphelion season (Ls 0-180). It is above 3 at the peak of global dust storms (record of 7 landers on the surface). Dust is in the sky all year. Earth: the global mean optical depth at 550 nm is approximately 0.1-0.2. This Earth figure is from memory and is not checked.
mars_environment.json.Not a share of clear days. It is the sha: This is not a share of clear days. It is the share of top-of-atmosphere sunlight that gets to level ground in a mean day, with cloud, haze and air together.
mars_environment.json.Not dust alone and not dust on the groun: This is not dust alone, and it is not dust on the ground. It is the optical depth at 550 nm of all fine particles in the air column together. These are dust, smoke, sea salt, haze and pollution, as a monthly mean for a 1 degree box.
mars_environment.json.Not sunlight at the ground: what a level: This is not sunlight at the ground. It is what a level surface would get above the atmosphere. We keep it to compare the ground figures with it.
mars_environment.json.Not what reaches the ground on a typical: This is not what reaches the ground on a typical day. It is what would reach a level surface on the same days if there were no cloud.
mars_environment.json.UV, sunlight at the ground, clear-sky da: This file gives UV, sunlight at the ground, clear-sky days and haze for each ranked square of the Mars part.
mars_environment.json.literature, not checked against a saved: From the literature, not checked against a saved file in this run. Mars: Cockell et al. 2000, Icarus 146, 343-359. Earth: the ozone cut-off near 290 nm.
mars_environment.json.nm, shortest wavelength of sunlight reac: nm, the shortest wavelength of sunlight that reaches the ground
mars_environment.json.none: the Mars source carries no cloud a: There is no fallback. The Mars source has no cloud amount, thus an unknown count of clear days stays unknown.

The UV index of the brightest hour (uv_index_brightest_hour) is the highest hourly value of ALLSKY_SFC_UV_INDEX_HR for the mean day of each month.
